key_responsibilities: Tune feedback parameters on robot hardware

strengths: Interrupt-driven real-time C: Robocon robot decodes quadrature encoders from first principles via a 4-bit A/B state machine on hardware interrupts and drives 4 motors at 15 kHz PWM; STM32 bare-metal timer/ADC/I2C firmware
Closed-loop feedback on real hardware: Robocon heading correction feeds encoder-derived angular error back into rotation PWM (the closest thing to the JD's 'tune feedback on robot hardware')
Robotics theory: hand-derived DH tables and FK chains for 6-DoF UR5e and 5-DoF AL5B, two-link IK on Arduino, SE(3) math engine, measured <2mm repeatability
Concurrency primitives in embedded code: FreeRTOS mutexes in the turret project; multiprocessing frame capture; MPI workers
Lab equipment: oscilloscopes, logic and spectrum analyzers, multimeters; DSP coursework
real_gaps: No MATLAB/Simulink anywhere in the profile, and it is a named core tool of the role
No classical control design evidence: no PID tuning method, loop shaping, Bode/stability margins, state-space or observer work
No vibration analysis, payload vibration, or structural dynamics work
No system identification or dynamic performance characterization (step/frequency response measurements)
No Java, no production robot-controller experience, no customer-site integration; seniority is capstone/internship scope
overstated_by_keywords: Control Theory and Dynamic Systems counted Adjacent via 'Closed-Loop Feedback Control' but that is simple heading-error P-style correction, not designed or analyzed control
Signal Analyzers counted Adjacent via 'Spectrum Analyzers' listed as a tool, with no bullet showing dynamic signal analyzer use for frequency-response work
Motion Control counted Adjacent but is open-loop servo PWM and IK, not trajectory or servo-loop design
understated_by_keywords: Digital filtering: custom sym6+bior3.5 wavelet bank for low-frequency noise suppression at BARC (PSNR 65 to 86) is real filter design, though on images rather than motion signals
Encoder odometry plus fixed-point QAT work shows comfort with sampled-data, fixed-point numerics relevant to controller firmware
screening_gaps: No MATLAB or controls toolbox experience for a MATLAB-centred role
No demonstrated control design or loop tuning with stability analysis (Bode, margins, state-space)
No vibration analysis or dynamic characterization of a mechanical system
llm_analysis.reasoning: The role's core is classical motion-control design, tuning and vibration characterization in MATLAB, and the profile has almost none of that. What it does have is strong real-time interrupt-driven C/C++, robotics kinematics and one genuine encoder-feedback loop, which covers the firmware and robotics-theory slice only. The posting is entry-compatible (MS plus 1 year), so this is a skills-depth gap rather than a seniority one; it is a long shot, not a clear no.
